topIssues.title: op-node, kona: Subtract simultaneous upgrade gas allocations
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:**

Karst and Lagoon can activate at the same timestamp while preserving fork order.

Both clients add both upgrade gas allocations to that activation block. Both reconstruction helpers stop after subtracting the Karst allocation.

The reconstructed system configuration retains the Lagoon allocation for later blocks.

The specification states: “The block after the activation block therefore returns to the chain's configured gas limit.”

Specification: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/blob/b733da804eeadc597c690f16601091e97af1fc68/specs/protocol/l2-upgrades-1-execution.md#reverting-the-allocation

Affected code:

- `op-node/rollup/derive/attributes.go:163-182`
- `op-node/rollup/derive/payload_util.go:67-84`
- `rust/kona/crates/protocol/derive/src/attributes/stateful.rs:190-219`
- `rust/kona/crates/protocol/protocol/src/utils.rs:107-130`

Trigger:

- Enable every predecessor through Karst.
- Set `KarstTime == LagoonTime` after genesis.
- Keep `KeepKarstUpgradeGas` disabled.
- Do not apply a same-origin gas update.

A focused reproduction stripped `55,370,657` gas instead of `116,023,829` gas. The resulting configuration retained `60,653,172` gas.

This changes later block capacity and base-fee behavior.

The reconstruction must subtract every matching activation allocation.

topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: port op-e2e conductor system coverage
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
## Summary

Port the user-visible conductor behaviors currently covered by `op-e2e/system/conductor` into `op-acceptance-tests` and the `op-devstack` DSL.

The existing acceptance coverage at `op-acceptance-tests/tests/base/conductor/leadership_transfer_test.go` only checks Raft membership, manual leadership transfer, and health. The older `op-e2e/system/conductor` package additionally covers sequencer activation, failover, disaster recovery, proxy behavior, and admin RPC behavior.

Acceptance tests are the better long-term home for these full-stack requirements, and will allow the same scenarios to be reused across CL implementations.

## Existing coverage to evaluate

- `op-e2e/system/conductor/sequencer_failover_test.go`
- `op-e2e/system/conductor/sequencer_failover_setup.go`
- `op-e2e/system/conductor/system_adminrpc_test.go`
- `op-acceptance-tests/tests/base/conductor/leadership_transfer_test.go`

## Scope

Port behaviors rather than copying the existing monolithic tests verbatim. Following the acceptance-test convention of one behavior per test, add coverage for at least:

- a conductor cluster starting with exactly one active sequencer;
- manual leadership transfer stopping the old sequencer and starting the target sequencer;
- unsafe block production continuing after leadership transfer, with nodes converging on the same hashes;
- active sequencer failure causing failover to a healthy replacement;
- disaster-recovery leader override;
- conductor RPC proxying serving only the active leader;
- relevant conductor membership operations and configuration-version checks.

Evaluate the generic admin RPC tests separately:

- sequencer start/stop and `admin_postUnsafePayload` are useful CL conformance behaviors;
- sequencer-state persistence is not conductor-specific and may belong in separate acceptance coverage;
- low-level exhaustive Raft RPC testing may remain better suited to `op-conductor` integration tests.

## Implementation guidance

- Add conductor actions and verification methods to `op-devstack/dsl` rather than using raw RPC calls in test bodies.
- Put condition-based waits inside DSL methods; do not port fixed sleeps or hand-written retry loops.
- Keep each acceptance test focused on one user-visible behavior.
- Preserve the existing `op-e2e/system/conductor` coverage until acceptance coverage parity and CI stability are demonstrated.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The selected `op-e2e/system/conductor` behaviors have equivalent acceptance tests.
- [ ] Leadership transfer verifies sequencer active-state transitions, block progression, and hash convergence—not only Raft leadership.
- [ ] Tests use the devstack DSL with bounded post-condition waits and no fixed sleeps.
- [ ] The tests run against the existing op-node conductor preset in CI.
- [ ] A coverage map documents which old tests were ported, intentionally retained, or intentionally replaced by lower-level tests.
- [ ] Redundant `op-e2e/system/conductor` tests are removed only after parity is established.

## Related

- #16418
- `docs/ai/writing-acceptance-tests.md`
- `docs/ai/flake-prevention.md`

topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestSequencerFailover_ConductorRPC` — hangs until 20m package timeout, panics op-e2e/system/conductor
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** `TestSequencerFailover_ConductorRPC` hung until the 20-minute package timeout, taking down the whole `op-e2e/system/conductor` package (`TestMain` panics, remaining tests in the binary never run, and gotestsum aborts the rerun with `rerun aborted because previous run had a suspected panic`).

**CI run:** https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5388221 (job `go-tests-short`)
**Date:** 2026-07-29
**Encountered on:** ethereum-optimism/optimism#22034, a Solidity-only branch (4 files, all under `packages/contracts-bedrock`). `go-tests-short` passed on the immediately preceding push of the same branch, and is green on `develop`.

```
panic: test timed out after 20m0s
	running tests:
		TestSequencerFailover_ConductorRPC (20m0s)

goroutine 14 [sync.WaitGroup.Wait, 19 minutes]:
sync.(*WaitGroup).Wait(0x6de78667648)
github.com/hashicorp/raft.(*raftState).waitShutdown(...)
	raft@v1.7.3/state.go:154
github.com/hashicorp/raft.(*shutdownFuture).Error(0x6de77c000d0)
	raft@v1.7.3/future.go:175 +0x29
github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-conductor/consensus.(*RaftConsensus).Shutdown(0x6de6969dae0)
	op-conductor/consensus/raft.go:297 +0x2e
github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-conductor/conductor.(*OpConductor).Stop(...)
```

The cluster never re-forms a quorum. `sequencer1` is gone (`dial tcp 127.0.0.1:36493: connect: connection refused`) and `sequencer2` never answers (`msgpack decode error [pos 0]: ... i/o timeout`), so `sequencer3` spins in pre-vote at a fixed `term=411` for the remaining ~6 minutes of log:

```
[WARN]  raft: Election timeout reached, restarting election
[INFO]  raft: entering candidate state: node="Node at 127.0.0.1:43037 [Candidate]" term=411
[DEBUG] raft: calculated votes needed: needed=2 term=411
[DEBUG] raft: pre-vote granted: from=sequencer3 term=411 tally=1
[ERROR] raft: failed to make requestVote RPC: target="{Voter sequencer1 ...}" error="dial tcp ...: connection refused" term=411
[DEBUG] raft: pre-vote denied: from=sequencer1 term=411 tally=1
```

Two things worth separating in an investigation:

1. Why the test wedges — a 2-of-3 quorum loss with one peer refusing connections and one timing out mid-msgpack.
2. `RaftConsensus.Shutdown` blocking forever on `waitShutdown`. Even once the test gives up, teardown can't complete, which is what converts a single stuck test into a whole-package panic and a lost rerun. A bounded shutdown would at least contain the blast radius.

topPRs.title: interop: suspend atomic demo router execution
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #22840. The atomic demo now supports nested cross-chain callbacks while retaining one live OP EVM transaction per chain. A on chain A calls B on chain B; B uses the same facade/router mechanism to call a distinct C on chain A; C sees A's pending state and can call back into the still-running B. The callback executes inside each chain's original transaction, preserving pending storage, transient storage, origin, gas ancestry and rollback. Each included chain receives one final replay after callback/result tapes and access lists are materialized; divergence rejects the candidate without discovery restarts or padding.

Canonical callback dispatch runs through ordinary router bytecode. Gas remains local to each chain: top-level application calls have fixed budgets, while callbacks receive half the remaining gas at their dispatch point. Caller context is restored on return, scheduling depth is capped at 32, and the bundle-wide call limit still applies. Failed callback hints force application rollback even if caught. ERC-4337 uses the existing EntryPoint and demo paymaster for normal on-chain gas settlement; it does not reimburse off-chain discovery or prove that a builder honestly attempted success. Existing Go and Kona cycle algorithms remain unchanged.

The Go/devstack bridge uses pinned candidate-prefix state and exact signed envelopes. This is a **demo node integration**; production payload-service admission/publication and a single-signature wallet flow remain out of scope. ETH forwarding, STATICCALL facades and committing after a caught remote failure remain unsupported. The original Go discovery path remains available for root-driven calls; nested dispatch is connected to the suspended builder.

Validation passed: all 18 contracts PR checks; full developer contract suite (2,290 passed, 183 skipped) and optimized suite (2,350 passed, 159 skipped); all 40 Rust builder tests with artifact-dependent tests enabled, including optimized bytecode; full Rust workspace lint/rustdoc and Go lint; Go bridge/message/filter/verifier tests; and Go/Kona nested-cycle regressions. All four real-node suspended/nested ERC-4337 success/revert cases pass, including exact receipt gas/log parity and sponsor settlement. Contract checks used the configured Foundry remappings plus explicit Solady/OpenZeppelin mappings with automatic remapping disabled to avoid the local duplicate `src/src` import issue.

Solidity, Rust lifecycle/application-effect and Go reviews are complete; all findings were fixed, none dismissed. Shared node fixtures are included by the normal contracts artifact build. #22840's branch remains unchanged.

CI on `ac7332b5d4af30420badf96e670243ec59df941d` is complete but not green: title/dependency checks and five Wiz scanners passed; Wiz SAST was skipped. The x86 multicannon package built, then [artifact attestation failed because the fork workflow lacks `id-token` permission](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/actions/runs/34524915489/job/103031802906), reproducing the previous head's permission failure. The other seven package jobs were canceled by fail-fast; image/smoke jobs were skipped. Full upstream CI for this fork still requires human authorization.

topPRs.title: feat: interop message-expiry refunds (censorship escape hatch for SuperchainETHBridge)
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
# feat: interop message-expiry refunds (censorship escape hatch for SuperchainETHBridge)

## Problem

Interop **executing messages cannot be force-included via deposit transactions** — `CrossL2Inbox.validateMessage` requires the message checksum slot to be warm via the tx's EIP-2930 access list, and deposits have no access list (upstream even added an explicit `CrossL2Inbox_NoExecutingDeposits` guard). So the force-inclusion path that normally defeats sequencer censorship does **not** work for interop: if a destination sequencer refuses to relay an executing message, delivery is impossible.

For `SuperchainETHBridge.sendETH` this strands funds: the ETH is burned into `ETHLiquidity` on the **source** before the message is sent, and only minted on the destination inside `relayETH`. A censored relay means the ETH is burned on A and never minted on B — permanently in flight, with no way for the sender to recover it. Interop ETH therefore lacks the "always recoverable to the sender" property that L1↔L2 bridging has.

## Key protocol fact this builds on

`MESSAGE_EXPIRY_WINDOW` (7 days, per-depset configurable) is a **protocol validity rule**, enforced both at cross-safety (op-supernode invalidates heads carrying expired executing messages) and **in the fault proof** (kona's `MessageGraph` forces a deposit-only replacement block). Once a destination chain's clock passes `initiatingTimestamp + window` with the message still unrelayed, **delivery is permanently impossible** — no valid block can ever relay it. This PR turns that permanent fact into a recoverable refund, riding only existing censorship-resistant rails (withdrawals and deposits). It does **not** add any new expiry machinery and does **not** modify `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger`.

## Mechanism

For a message `H` sent A→B that was never relayed on B:

1. **B (attest)** — anyone calls `MessageExpiryRelay.attestUndelivered(H, sourceChainId, minGas)`. The relay checks the local `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger.successfulMessages(H) == false` and exports `(H, sourceChainId, block.timestamp)` to the `MessageExpiryHub` on L1 via B's ordinary L2→L1 withdrawal. (This is *not* an executing message, so if B censors it, it is itself force-includable as a deposit.)
2. **L1 (route)** — after the withdrawal finalizes, `MessageExpiryHub.receiveExpiryNotice` authenticates the calling L1CrossDomainMessenger and its cluster, records the notice, then `forwardExpiryNotice` deposits it into the source chain via A's L1CrossDomainMessenger (force-includable).
3. **A (consume)** — `MessageExpiryRelay.receiveExpiry` verifies the attestation against the recorded send: the attestor must equal the recorded destination and `attestedAt` must be strictly beyond `recordedAt + expiryWindow`. It then notifies the sending application once.
4. **App (refund)** — `SuperchainETHBridge.onMessageExpired` re-mints the burned ETH and force-sends it back to the original sender.

**No double-spend:** the attestation only exists if `H` was undelivered; the refund only fires once `attestedAt > recordedAt + expiryWindow`; past the window, delivery is protocol-impossible; and both the relay record and the bridge's pending-send entry are deleted before any external call. Delivery and refund are mutually exclusive.

## Reusable primitive

The escape hatch is **not** ETH-bridge-specific. Any L2 contract that sends interop messages can opt in:
- call `MessageExpiryRelay.recordSentMessage(...)` when it sends (preimage-verified, so only the actual sender can register as the handler for a message hash), and
- implement `IMessageExpiryHandler.onMessageExpired(msgHash, attestorChainId, attestedAt)` to compensate.

`SuperchainETHBridge` is the first consumer and the reference integration.

## SuperchainETHBridge diff (minimal)

`1.0.1 → 1.1.0`. `sendETH` records the pending send and registers with the relay (guarded by a code-size check so non-interop chains are unaffected); new `onMessageExpired` refunds the sender. `relayETH` and everything else are untouched. The contract previously had zero storage; `pendingETHSends` is added at slot 0.

## New contracts

- `src/L2/MessageExpiryRelay.sol` — predeploy `0x42…2E` (proxied, interop-gated), both source-side (record/receive) and destination-side (attest) roles; same address on every chain.
- `src/L1/MessageExpiryHub.sol` — ownerless L1 singleton that routes notices between the chains of an interop cluster. Cluster membership is derived on-chain per call (SystemConfig ↔ L1CrossDomainMessenger ↔ OptimismPortal bidirectional binding + shared ETHLockbox authorization + shared AnchorStateRegistry); notices are namespaced by the cluster's lockbox so chains with colliding IDs across clusters cannot interfere.
- `interfaces/L2/IMessageExpiryHandler.sol` — the opt-in callback interface.

Predeploy wired through `Predeploys.sol`, `L2ContractsManager` (`→ 1.15.0`), `L2Genesis`, the Go predeploy registry, and the NUT upgrade bundle. The relay proxy ships **uninitialized** (fails closed); `hub`/`expiryWindow` are set post-deploy by the ProxyAdmin owner.

## Testing

- **Unit (forge):** full auth + boundary matrices for all three contracts, including sender-binding, exact expiry off-by-one, cross-cluster non-interference, and the refund end-state. (~70 tests.)
- **Acceptance (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/expiry`, in-process two-chain interop devnet):** end-to-end — `sendETH` A→B, never relay, wait past a 12s expiry window, attest on B, prove + finalize the withdrawal on L1, forward through the hub, deposit into A, assert the sender is refunded exactly and all records are cleared. Plus a delivered-message regression guard (normal relay still works on the 1.1.0 bridge, and attesting a delivered message reverts). Runs without time-travel by shrinking the L1 dispute windows via new deployer options.

## Security

Two independent adversarial reviews were run. Both found the same **critical** in an earlier revision — the hub authenticated the incoming messenger but not the portal, letting a forged SystemConfig point at a real cluster-authorized portal and mint a false notice. **Fixed** by binding `portal.systemConfig() == systemConfig` (plus a registration-overwrite guard, notice-key namespacing by source chain, an attestation-timestamp bound, a monotone `expiryWindow` setter + `hub` setter for remediation, and a contract-handler requirement). Details and the list of attacks that were tried and failed are in the review notes.

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **Deploy/init wiring:** this is contracts-first. A production rollout needs a deploy script for `MessageExpiryHub` and an OPCM/governance step to `initialize` each relay proxy (`hub`, `expiryWindow`). The feature fails closed until then.
- **`expiryWindow` ↔ depset coupling:** the relay's window must be ≥ the dependency-set message-expiry window, but there is no on-chain link on L2 today (it is trusted ProxyAdmin-owner config, guarded only by the monotone setter). When the protocol exposes the depset window on-chain, self-validate.
- **Hub guardian pause:** considered as an incident kill-switch, deliberately omitted to avoid adding a trust role to an ownerless singleton; remediation today is re-pointing relays via `setHub`.
- Cluster liquidity/ASR migrations strand pending notices until re-attested (multi-day, recoverable).

topPRs.title: kona-sp1: add multi-cycle proposer policy scenarios
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds comprehensive multi-cycle proposer policy coverage using the deterministic `ScenarioWorld` and `ScenarioHarness`.

The scenarios cover:

- Frozen proposal horizons and long foreign-game histories
- Concurrent defense while creation is stalled
- Trusted and untrusted superroot contradictions
- Timed-out creation, late inclusion, and duplicate-creation guards
- Invalid topology, ownership, resolution, claim, and payout policy
- Independent pinned L1, latest L1, host, safe, and finalized clocks
- Factory, pending-game, and cached-game read-failure isolation
- Fresh proposer reconstruction over existing confirmed history

The scenario world now supports:

- L1 read faults keyed by boundary, target, and attempt
- Superroot query journaling with trust and L1 metadata
- Fresh proposer restarts over persistent world state
- Small history mutation controls required by the policy scenarios

The scenarios also exposed and fix a creation-safety issue:

- Game creation now requires a trusted superroot response before querying the UUID or submitting a bonded transaction.
- Trusted claim mismatches are terminal regardless of creator; untrusted observations remain retryable.
- The duplicate-creation guard is cleared when its tracked game becomes terminal or when factory history resets.

Treating a trusted contradiction as terminal may immediately release the creation guard and allow a
replacement at the same timestamp, putting a second bond at risk if the trusted response itself is
wrong. This is intentional: trusted supernode responses are the proposer's canonicality boundary;
retaining the guard would otherwise block recovery indefinitely at a frozen horizon.

Proof deadlines continue to use latest L1 chain time, matching the on-chain `block.timestamp` deadline check.

No launch, devstack, or acceptance-test configuration changes are required.

topPRs.title: kona!: add chain_id metric label
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
_Requested by **Sebastian Stammler** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1787240090382769)_

Part of #22529.

**Before.** kona's metrics carry no chain dimension. In a single-chain kona-node that is fine, but in a multi-chain lokahi process every chain's series collapse into one — `kona_node_block_labels{label="unsafe"}` would flap between chains instead of showing each one.

**After.** Every metric emitted by kona's `engine`, `gossip`, `disc`, `rpc`, `derive`, `providers-local`, `providers-alloy` and `node-service` crates carries a `chain_id` label. No metric is renamed; one metric's label set changes, see below.

**How.** Each metric owner already has its chain ID (or its `RollupConfig`) in scope, so the label is threaded from what is already there rather than plumbed in: `EngineState` gains a `chain_id` field, long-lived components cache an `Arc<str>` label instead of formatting per emit, and `Metrics::init`/`zero` take the chain ID so the pre-created series are labelled too. The label key and its `Arc<str>` constructor live in `kona-macros`, so the seven `Metrics` types share one spelling rather than seven. `set!` and `record!` gained variadic-label arms — only `inc!` had one, so no `set!`/`record!` site could express two labels.

**Drift found on the way.** Labelling `zero()` meant walking every pre-created series against its emit sites, and a number of them disagreed: `dial_peer_error`, `find_node_requests`, `gossip_events`, `rpc_calls`, `chain_rpc_calls`, the engine task list (the `seal` task was missing), the `block_validation_failed` reasons (`parent_beacon_root` is produced by no error arm), and the beacon-client, L2-provider and buffered-provider method strings now all match what is emitted. `banned_peers` is no longer pre-created, since its `peer_id` has no finite value set. `kona_node_gossipsub_events`, `kona_providers_local_cache_capacity` and `kona_providers_cache_memory_bytes` were pre-created but never emitted by anything, and are removed rather than multiplied by the number of chains. Three components also still emitted process-wide: the node builds one `OnlineBeaconClient` and one `OnlineBlobProvider` per chain, and `BlobSource`/`CalldataSource` already receive the `RollupConfig`, so all four take the chain ID now.

BREAKING CHANGE: `kona_node_engine_task_failure` changes shape. It previously used the task name as the label *key* with the severity as its value (`{insert="critical"}`), so every task type minted a new label key and the series `Metrics::zero()` pre-created was never the one incremented. It now emits `{type="insert",severity="critical",chain_id="..."}`, matching `kona_node_engine_task_count`. Operators with panels or alert rules selecting `kona_node_engine_task_failure{insert=...}` (or `consolidate`/`build`/`finalize`) must migrate them to `{type="insert",severity="critical"}`. No in-repo Grafana dashboard selects this metric, so the blast radius is external dashboards only.

BREAKING CHANGE: the Rust API of the affected crates changes too, for downstream consumers who depend on them directly.

- Three public constants are removed: `Metrics::GOSSIPSUB_EVENT` (`kona-gossip`), `Metrics::CACHE_CAPACITY` (`kona-providers-local`) and `Metrics::CACHE_MEMORY_USAGE` (`kona-providers-alloy`). No time series disappears with them — nothing in the workspace ever emitted any of the three.
- `Metrics::init()` and `Metrics::zero()` now take a `chain_id: u64` on all seven `Metrics` types, and about twenty component constructors gain the same parameter, several of them losing `const` to build the label. The ones most likely to be constructed downstream are `BlobSource::new`, `CalldataSource::new`, `AlloyChainProvider::new`/`new_http`/`new_with_trust`, `ConnectionGater::new` and the `kona-derive` stage constructors. (`AlloyL2ChainProvider` is unaffected — it already took the `RollupConfig`.)
- `EngineSyncState::apply_update` is now module-private; use `EngineState::apply_sync_update(update)`, which supplies the chain ID from the state it already holds.
- `OnlineBlobProvider` and `OnlineBeaconClient` are the exception: they gain a `with_chain_id(chain_id)` builder method and a public field, so existing construction keeps compiling unchanged.

---
